speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history suggestive of bone fragility; can you tell me more specifically about your growth history and any fractures you have experienced?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (11β-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly) at birth, virilization (maternal hirsutism, severe acne), and bone fragility due to cortisol deficiency strongly points to this specific enzyme deficiency. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone and Serum Cortisol levels.
